status_note: The house 'how to measure' sheets draw a stack of horizontal rings on a reference figure, each labelled in inches. This file declares that stack as a PROTOCOL — which heights to look at, relative to which registry landmark — so the viewer can draw the same rings on this avatar. A level is a reference height, not a POM: it is not measured against a tolerance, it has no house code, it appears in no POM sheet, and it is not a fit recommendation. The girth the viewer reports at a level is the ordinary section girth of this body at that height (convex hull, as everywhere else), reported so the person can read the body, not so anything is graded.
declared_limit: Reference levels are heights from the underbust line, not a fit recommendation and not a size.

datum.comment: The 0 line on the sheets is drawn in black and carries no printed label. Reading it as the underbust line is an INTERPRETATION. It is drawn at the inframammary fold on all three sheets — that part a person read off the drawing, and the trace script deliberately does not pretend to have detected it (ink over skin is the same brown as the shadow under the breast). What the trace does verify is the other half: the thirteen printed values fit a linear inch scale whose zero falls inside the sheets' one unlabelled gap, between the +1/2in and -1in leaders, on all three sheets. UNDERBUST_FOLD is the registry's landmark for that height and is detected automatically, so the whole stack resolves without a hand-placed point. If the house says the black line is something else, change this field: nothing else in the stack moves.
datum.alternatives_considered: BUST_LEVEL was ruled out — the sheets draw no ring at the apex at all, and the printed values would then be neither monotonic nor centred on it.

unit.comment: Offsets are declared in inches because that is what the sheets print. Level height = datum height + offset_in * 0.0254, in the GLB's metres.

reliability.comment: The torso surface is open at the armhole, so sections above y = 1.39m are unreliable (MEASUREMENT_PLAN.md section 4.3, and the registry's scan note). A level above it must report that it is out of range rather than a girth. On this asset the top level (+4 1/4in above a fold at y = 1.265m) lands at y = 1.373m, 14mm clear of the armhole's lowest point (y = 1.387m).

source_note: Copied unchanged from '3D How to Measure' (Adobe Illustrator document '3D measurements', 2026-08-28). The figure on them is a reference body, NOT this avatar: nothing about its dimensions transfers, only which heights the house looks at and what they are called.

upper.comment: Above the breast; the sheets draw these in violet.

root.comment: Across the lower breast between the fold and the apex; the sheets draw these in orange.

lower.comment: Below the fold toward the waist; violet on the sheets.

levels_note: Fourteen rings: thirteen printed values and the unlabelled 0. The sheets draw nothing across the bust apex — the gap between +1 1/4in and +3 1/2in is the sheets', not an omission here. The printed values are the authority; the pixel trace is the check on them.
tape_note: A level with "tape": true is also drawn as a red tape, with a row under the underbust in the measurement table, wherever the POM tapes are (asked for 2026-09-27 for -1 1/2in and -1 3/4in). It stays a level, not a POM: the girth is the section at that height, with no house code and no POM-sheet row.

shapes.label_en: Centre-back rectangle, 1 3/4in wide and 2 7/8in tall, standing on the -1 3/4in level
shapes.comment: Asked for 2026-09-27: the midpoint of the bottom edge is the centre back of the -1 3/4in ring. Every side is measured along the skin, as a tape would lie: the bottom edge along the ring, the sides straight up the back, the top edge along the section the sides reach (its own length is reported, not forced). Drawn in red with a row under the -1 3/4in tape. A reference shape, not a POM: no house code, no POM-sheet row.

reference_tapes_note: Tapes parallel to the largest girth, 2in and 3in above it (asked for 2026-09-27). They hang on that POM's own height, found by the scan, not on the underbust datum, and they are not part of the sheets' stack. On this asset both land above the armhole (max girth at y = 1.355m, so y = 1.406m and 1.431m; the armhole's lowest point is 1.387m): the torso is open there, so each is drawn as the front and back pieces of the section on the skin, with their lengths, and no girth.
lines_note: A line straight down the centre back from the Max +2in tape to the -1 1/2in ring (asked for 2026-09-27): the body cut by the centre plane x = 0, followed on the skin between the two centre-back points, so its length is what a tape laid down the spine reads. The straight chord between the ends is reported beside it. A second line runs straight up the centre front from the -1 3/4in ring to the height of the largest girth (DIAG_MAX_TORSO_GIRTH, the scan's own height, asked for 2026-09-27): the same cut x = 0, followed on the skin up the breastbone from the ring's centre front until it reaches that height. It ends on the skin, between the breasts; the max-girth tape itself lies across the breasts there, in front of it (33mm in front on this asset).
ticks_note: Blue marks 5mm long across the Max +2in tape (asked for 2026-09-27): 4in from its centre back on each side, and 4 3/8in from its centre front on each side. The distance is walked along the tape's own section (on the back, or on the front); each mark stands upright across the tape (the vertical cut through its point, followed on the skin 2.5mm up and 2.5mm down), so it reads square to the tape from the front or the back.
straps_note: A band 2cm wide from each front tick over the shoulder to the back tick on the same side (asked for 2026-09-27), as a strap would lie. Its two ends are on the Max +2in tape, 1cm each way along it from the tick, so each end is centred on its tick and exactly 2cm wide. Each long edge is the body cut by the upright plane through its front and back corner, followed on the skin over the shoulder; it must arrive at its back corner or the strap is not drawn. The strap's length is its middle, from tick to tick over the shoulder in the upright plane through the two ticks (asked for 2026-09-27), with its own row; the two edges' lengths are reported beside it. The width over the shoulder is what the two edges leave there, reported, not forced. On the front the strap now starts at the Max +3in tape instead (front_on, asked for 2026-09-27), in the same place: its middle stays the upright plane through the two ticks, and the front end is centred where that middle crosses Max +3in, 1cm each way along it, so both ends are still exactly 2cm. The length runs along the middle from there. A reference shape, not a POM.
curves_note: The cup armhole (asked for 2026-09-27): a curve on the skin from the outer front corner of the shoulder strap (on the Max +3in tape) to the top of the wing height on the same side (SIDE_WING_HIGH_L / _R, the side point of the max-girth section). It is shaped with two tangent handles, one at each end (asked for 2026-09-27, so the armhole can be drawn as wanted): the curve is the cubic Bezier through the two ends and the two handle tips, carried onto the skin, and its length is that line on the skin, what a tape laid along the drawn armhole reads. It passes through the armhole point (through, asked for 2026-09-27): the curve is then two Beziers joined there smoothly, the tangent at the point being the chord from end to end laid in the skin, each side of it a third of its own segment's chord long. Each end handle is an angle and a length read square to the skin's normal at its end: 0 deg points along the shortest path over the skin from that end to the armhole point (the model the pen and the wing height use), positive turns it up toward the shoulder. The values here are the default, 0 deg at both ends, 30mm at the strap and 11mm at the wing (about a third of each segment's shortest path); in the viewer the handle tips are dragged on the body, one pair shaping both sides mirrored, and the length updates as they move. A dragged shape is the viewer's, not this file's, until it is written here. A reference line, not a POM. The second curve, CF → strap (asked for 2026-09-28), runs on each side from the top of the centre-front line (on the centre plane, so both sides start at the same point) to the strap's front inner corner on the Max +3in tape. It is a joined_curve (made smarter the same day): its ends take their direction from what they join. At the strap it arrives along the strap's inner edge, so the two read as one line running on over the shoulder. At the centre front it leaves level, the two sides meeting smoothly in a U (handles.cf.angle_deg 0), or rising at an angle in the skin for a V (up to 75 deg). With both directions set, one number shapes it, handles.depth.fullness: how far along each end tangent, toward where the two tangents meet, the Bezier's inner points lie (0.667 is the parabola through that meeting point; less is flatter, more a deeper scoop). Each sample is carried onto the skin at its own height (the level section through it), so seen from the front the curve is the one drafted and a U stays level into the cleavage. The nearest point of each level section jumps about a little from one height to the next (smoothed 2026-09-28, it had kinks of up to 1.5mm over the top of the bust), so the run is then eased across the body: six times, each sample a quarter of the way toward each neighbour in x and z, its height kept, the last few samples held so it still runs into the strap along the strap's edge. That moves no sample more than 1.2mm. On this asset the default (U, 0.667) is 166.4mm on each side and bows 46.4mm below the shortest path over the skin (131.9mm). In the viewer the dot at the centre front sets the angle (near level snaps to U) and the dot in the middle the fullness, both sides mirrored. The wire (asked for 2026-09-28) is drawn in red on each side, from the armhole mark to the CF point, where the two sides meet. Since 2026-09-28 (asked the same day: 'follow the breast root exactly') it follows the breast root in between: the crease where the breast leaves the chest wall, found about the apex (root.about, BUST_APEX_L / _R; src/features/reference_geometry/root.mjs). The root is read off the skin as its most concave line: at each vertex the mean curvature (half the cotangent Laplacian along the vertex normal; none on a cut of the surface), and on each profile about the apex, one per degree (the skin cut by the plane through the apex holding the forward direction, at that angle from straight down, followed out to the centre plane or to its farthest point from the apex in its direction), the profile's first concave stretch out from the apex and its least point, refined by a parabola. The root is the run of profiles with one that holds straight down, so it ends where the crease runs out; on this asset it runs out 56deg outward of straight down, where the breast merges into the side, and inward it reaches the centre plane, where the two breasts meet. Each profile's root is read off one mesh edge, so the run is eased along itself (the distance from the apex on each profile, twelve times) and put back on its own profile. The wire follows it from its outer end inward, until the next profile's root would rise past the CF point's height or reach the centre plane, and joins each end to it round the body (angle about the upright axis through the middle of the body, and height): a cubic Bezier leaving the root along its own direction, a third of the join's chord long, not bending at the armhole mark and drawn arriving level at the CF point, so neither side crosses the centre plane; each join sample carried out along its level ray to the skin. The joined run is spaced evenly (2.5mm) and eased along itself sixteen times in all three directions, its ends kept: the root's heights are read facet by facet and carry the mesh's noise, and carried back to the nearest skin afterwards the facets' edges put the kinks back. The wire no longer passes through ROOT_BOTTOM (the fold point below the apex, where cup depth starts; decided 2026-09-28, the POM is unchanged): its lowest point is its own, and how far ROOT_BOTTOM is from it is reported. On this asset it is 243.0mm on each side, 144.3mm from the armhole mark to its lowest point (y = 1.2652m, 89.1mm out from the centre) and 98.6mm from there to the CF point; 125.9mm of it runs along the root, between 48deg inward and 56deg outward of straight down, at most 2.15mm off the root as found on any profile (half the mesh's median edge is 3.15mm); ROOT_BOTTOM is 2.98mm from it; the two sides meet in a V of 12.2deg. (The first version, two Beziers through the armhole mark, ROOT_BOTTOM and the CF point, was smooth but ran 9-17mm off the crease on both legs, and met in a V of 54deg.) Whenever the CF point slides along its line (it can be dragged from the wire's rows too) or the armhole is reshaped, carrying the armhole mark with it, the wire is drawn again; the root is found once per body and kept. Curves are measured in this list's order, with the dots on the curves before a wire placed first, so the wire comes after the cup armhole. The root it follows is drawn, not measured: it is not the BREAST_ROOT_ARC POM, whose inner and outer ends stay manual_only. A reference line, not a POM.
points_note: The armhole point, on each side (asked for 2026-09-27): 3/8in higher than the top of the wing height (SIDE_WING_HIGH_L / _R, the side point of the max-girth section) and 1 1/4in forward of there. Both distances are on the skin, as a tape measures on a form: first straight up the side (the upright cut through the wing top, square to the body's side), then toward the front along the level section at the height reached. The cup armhole passes through it. Drawn as a blue dot like the armhole, with a row; the values here are where it sits by default, and in the viewer it can be dragged on the skin (both sides, mirrored), the row then reading the up and forward offsets that reach the dragged place, and the armhole following it. A dragged place is the viewer's, not this file's, until it is written here. A reference point, not a POM. The CF point (asked for 2026-09-28) is a dot on the CF line, of kind on_line: up_in is how far up the line it sits from the line's lower end (the -1 3/4in ring), along the skin, as a tape laid up the line reads it; 2 5/8in by default, about halfway to the max-girth height. It lies on the line and only moves along it, and the line runs on the centre plane, so it is one dot, not a pair. Drawn as a blue dot with a row under the CF line reading that distance; in the viewer it can be dragged, from its own row or the CF line's, and it slides along the line and nowhere else (to the place on the line nearest the pointer on screen), stopping at the ends. A dragged place is the viewer's, not this file's, until it is written here. A reference point, not a POM. The armhole mark (asked for 2026-09-28) is a dot on the cup armhole, on each side, of kind on_curve: along_in is how far along the curve it sits from the curve's end named by end, here to, the top of the wing height (SIDE_WING_HIGH_L / _R), along the skin: 1 1/4in. It is not dragged. It rides on the armhole: whenever the armhole is reshaped (its handles dragged, or the armhole point moved) it is placed again the same distance along, and it is placed once the armhole is measured, so no curve may pass through it; the wire starts from it (see curves_note). On this asset it lands 1.8mm short of the armhole point, which is 33.6mm (1 5/16in) along the armhole from the wing top, so the two nearly coincide; it is drawn near-black, with a row under the armhole, so it reads apart from the blue armhole point beside it. A reference point, not a POM.

trace.comment: A budget for the sheets, not for this avatar: how far any one leader may sit from the sheet's own best-fit inch scale. Observed worst 0.269in (three-quarter sheet), which is draughting slack on a drawn diagram. The gate also requires the fitted zero to land inside the unlabelled gap on every sheet. Exceeding either means the reading of the sheets is wrong, not that the tolerance should be raised.

declared_limits: Reference levels are heights from the underbust line, not a fit recommendation and not a size.
The figure on the source sheets is not this avatar; only the protocol transfers, never a dimension.
That the black 0 line is the underbust line is an interpretation of an unlabelled mark, evidenced by the trace and recorded here so it can be corrected in one field.
A level's girth is a body dimension with no compression allowance, like every other girth in this project.
Levels are not POMs: no house code, no tolerance, no POM sheet row, no evidence in measurements.json.
